paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me: prayer lands. Hezekiah prayed about Sennacherib, and the very next thing we see is the LORD answering, "Because you have prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria…" (Isaiah 37:21). Hezekiah didn't have to sort it out himself. He brought it to the LORD, and the LORD took it from there.

Now look at Sennacherib. He talks like every city he crushed was his own doing, chariots and cedars and all. But the LORD says, "Long ago I ordained it; in days of old I planned it" (Isaiah 37:26). The LORD also says, "I know your sitting down, your going out and coming in, and your raging against Me" (Isaiah 37:28). Nobody is too big for Him, and nothing gets past Him.

So when something scary is standing over you, baker, you can do what Hezekiah did and pray. The LORD says, "I will defend this city and save it for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David" (Isaiah 37:35). He keeps His word, and He promised Hezekiah a harvest too, because "the zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this" (Isaiah 37:32). I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, I know how big a problem can feel. It's still no bigger than the One who answers.
